plan.name: Use bracketed repository paths literally
plan.summary: Allow [ and ] as literal characters in ordinary repository paths, including part directories, committed rules, documents and dependency inputs, planned and touched files, and init discovery, so dynamic route directories such as app/[slug] can be built. Keep refusing brackets in trusted and shared selectors and native acceptance file paths, preserve all other path restrictions and captured-base authority, and have init retain unresolved requirements wherever its existing selector rules still prevent a valid declaration. Make the factory's Git operations on named files and directories use literal pathspecs for staging, forced staging, deletions, exports, directory lookups and history, preserve intentional discovery patterns, and make the sandbox enumerate Go test files in literal directories. Ownership, plan digests, staging, diffs, scope, trust checks and sandbox runs must distinguish app/[slug]/page.tsx from app/s/page.tsx, never admitting or substituting the latter because it matches a pattern. Update SPEC.md and the linked docs/factory.md contract, init and native acceptance documentation to describe this distinction, with changed SPEC bullets citing [#877's ratified plan](.invariant/plans/issue-877.json).

tests.name: TestRepositoryOwnsLiteralBracketPaths877
tests.says: Ordinary bracketed declarations, reads, ownership and trust queries retain literal identity and captured bytes; new and deleted paths retain their owners, while selectors and unsafe paths remain refused.

tests.name: TestInitDiscoversBracketedRoutes877
tests.says: Init's read-only draft discovers bracketed routes, nested rules, current-state documents and part directories without telling users to rename them, and a complete route application draft loads with exact ownership.

tests.name: TestFactoryStagesOnlyTheLiteralBracketPath877
tests.says: Committing a bracketed file or directory, deleting its file, or force-adding an ignored written file stages only the literal selection and leaves its pattern-matching neighbor out.

tests.name: TestFactoryExportsAndFindsHistoryForOneBracketPath877
tests.says: Export includes only the named bracketed file or directory, and FirstCommit ignores an earlier change to its pattern-matching neighbor.

tests.name: TestNativePlanDigestKeepsBracketPathsLiteral877
tests.says: A native plan binds an ordinary bracketed production path to a distinct execution digest, rejects substitution by its neighbor, and still refuses brackets in acceptance file paths.

tests.name: TestBracketPlanStagesDiffsAndRunsOnlyItsOwner877
tests.says: Diff and staging admit only the planned bracketed route edit; a configured sandbox runs its owner's checks on that edit with the neighbor and original checkout preserved.

tests.name: TestSandboxFileListUsesLiteralBracketDirectories877
tests.says: The sandbox's Go file list includes the tests in the literal bracketed directory and excludes the tests in a directory that matches it as a glob.

tests.name: TestScopeKeepsBracketPathsAndTrustExact877
tests.says: Committed native scope accepts planned bracketed edits and deletions, refuses an unplanned neighbor, and retains captured trust for changed or deleted nested agent rules.
